rounds.text: Oval Projects Engineering Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a margin of safety calculated at 82.5% [E37]. The company demonstrates robust operational efficiency, evidenced by a return on capital employed of 20.3% [E12] and a return on equity of 16.0% [E13], both of which comfortably outperform their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. This performance is underpinned by strong growth momentum, as seen in the 45% compounded sales growth and 45% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E15, E17]. The market is currently pricing the stock at a P/E of 6.44x, which is less than half of the sector benchmark of 13.66x [E6], and a price-to-book ratio of 0.8x, also below the sector average [E7]. While the company has shown a multi-year sales uptrend and rising EPS [E46, E47], it is important to note that the share price has declined by 30% over the last year [E18]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating and free cash flow [E26, E27], increased working capital days [E44], and significant contingent liabilities [E43].

The most concerning aspect of Oval Projects Engineering Ltd is the severe disconnect between reported profits and actual cash generation. In March 2026, the company reported negative operating cash flow of Rs -37 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -47 Cr, resulting in a deeply troubling cash conversion ratio of -2.64x [E25, E26, E27]. This liquidity strain is compounded by a significant increase in working capital days, which have ballooned from 65.2 to 144 days, suggesting the company is struggling to collect on its sales [E44]. Furthermore, the company’s reliance on debt is rising, with borrowings climbing to Rs 87 Cr from Rs 75 Cr in the prior year [E30]. Investors should also note the substantial contingent liabilities of Rs 78.8 Cr, which represent a significant off-balance-sheet risk [E43]. While the stock has suffered a 30% decline in price over the last year [E18], the inconsistent operating margin trends over the last two years and two quarters suggest that the underlying business performance remains volatile [E23, E24]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong return on capital employed of 20.3% and has demonstrated robust compounded sales and profit growth [E12, E14, E16].

Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -37 Cr and free cash flow was Rs -47 Cr in March 2026, creating a cash conversion of -2.64x [E25, E26, E27]. However, this severe cash-flow period is completely detached from the company's powerful fundamental growth engine, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 36% and profit growth of 62% [E14, E16]. The bear highlights rising borrowings at Rs 87 Cr [E30], but ignores that this is supported by a comfortable short-term current ratio of 2.01x and a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74x [E28, E29]. Conceded: working capital days have increased to 144 days and contingent liabilities stand at Rs.78.8 Cr [E43, E44], yet the business still prints an exceptional ROCE of 20.3% and an ROE of 16% [E12, E13]. Finally, while the bear cites inconsistent operating margins and a 30% price drop [E18, E23, E24], the TTM operating margin has actually expanded by 3 percentage points to 16% [E22], and current pricing implies an absurd -6.4% earnings growth expectation that vastly underestimates the firm's robust operational reality [E38].

Conceded: 3-year compounded sales growth is 36% and profit growth is 62% [E14, E16]. However, this reported growth is entirely illusory from a cash perspective, as operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs -37 Cr and free cash flow to negative Rs -47 Cr in March 2026, driving a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -2.64x [E25, E26, E27]. Conceded: the current ratio sits at 2.01x [E29]. Yet, the bull's dismissal of balance sheet strain ignores that total borrowings expanded to Rs 87 Cr by September 2026, up from Rs 75 Cr a year prior [E30]. Conceded: ROCE stands at 20.3% and ROE at 16% [E12, E13]. Nevertheless, these accounting returns completely overlook the severe operational friction revealed by working capital days doubling from 65.2 days to 144 days alongside massive contingent liabilities of Rs 78.8 Cr [E43, E44]. Finally, while the bull points to TTM margin expansion and low market expectations [E22, E38], the yearly and quarterly operating margin trends are explicitly categorized as inconsistent, and the stock price has suffered a punishing 30% drop over the past year [E18, E23, E24].
